note:
Determined directly from gt_results/arvo_10140/vulnerable-instrumentation.patch, which shows Stage 04's actual ASSERT_EVT print markers inserted into the real vulnerable crypto/pem/pem_lib.c (hunks at original lines 625-641, matching ground_truth.json's cited lines 610/628/635-638/640): `i = BIO_gets(bp, buf, 254); fprintf(stderr, "ASSERT_EVT point=bio_gets_return bytes_written=%d
", i);` binds bio_gets_return.bytes_written to the variable `i` (BIO_gets' return value/byte count, stored in i); and `buf[++i] = '
'; buf[++i] = '\0'; fprintf(stderr, "ASSERT_EVT point=strncmp_site bytes_initialized=%d comparison_length=11
", i + 1);` immediately preceding `if (strncmp(buf, "-----BEGIN ", 11) == 0)` binds strncmp_site.comparison_length to the literal `11` (strncmp's third argument at line 640) and the observed-kind field bytes_initialized to the expression `i + 1` (count of initialized bytes right before the strncmp call). Cross-checked against gt_results/arvo_10140/vulnerable_assertion_trace.txt and fixed_assertion_trace.txt runtime values (bytes_written=1, bytes_initialized=2, comparison_length=11 for the 1-byte PoC: i=1 after BIO_gets, i+1=2 after the two buf[++i]= writes) and against assertion_results.json's TRANS-bio-gets-partial-write matrix (left=11, right=1). Only two of these four fields are actually consumed downstream: 'bio_gets_return.bytes_written' and 'strncmp_site.comparison_length' come from TRANS-bio-gets-partial-write, the sole kind:transition assertion in verified_assertions.json (no kind:required assertion survived verification -- REQ-buf-init-guard was dropped from verified_assertions.json per assertion_results.json's verified:false). The bare-keyed 'bytes_initialized' and 'comparison_length' entries are a harmless bonus binding for OBS-sink-uninit-read (kind:observed, not currently consumed by build_probes.py/questions.py at all -- confirmed no 'observed' handling path exists in either file); they're keyed without an event prefix because that assertion's raw check operands ($bytes_initialized, $comparison_length) never carried one to begin with, so this matches exactly what _resolve_operand's '$'-stripping would produce if that path were ever wired up. No field was omitted for lack of confidence; the vulnerable-instrumentation.patch/trace-file combination pinned down every field's real vulnerable-version source expression precisely, and patch.diff (the unrelated X509_verify fix) was not needed at all since it never touches pem_lib.c.
